privacyFacts: Encrypted storage does not hide deliberately submitted analysis text from the backend or model provider.
Approval requires an explicit human action; prompt-free signing does not grant autonomous approval.
Internal example applications are not independent developer adoption. No bounty, recovery demonstration or deployment is claimed complete.

Compromised same-origin code can read unlocked data; the CSP and in-memory keys reduce exposure but do not isolate it.

Recovery needs the original usable credential and rpId and the surviving ciphertext. A replayed older snapshot cannot be detected once all local state is lost, and erasure from storage or backups is not guaranteed. No security audit is claimed.

An assistant request carries the selected excerpts, the confirmed facts listed in its preview and a digest of the review inputs to the application server in readable form. eip712.typeString: ReviewAction(address reviewer,uint8 action,bytes32 commitment,bytes32 replacementCommitment,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
eip712.notes: Fields are hashed with abi.encode in declaration order and the digest comes from OpenZeppelin EIP712._hashTypedDataV4. It is never the Chapter 2 package digest, a bare struct hash or a personal_sign hash.

events.supersessionNote: One SUPERSEDE emits ReceiptIssued for the replacement (predecessor set) and then ReceiptSuperseded, in one transaction and with the same nonce. They are one atomic action: the replacement is counted once.

lifecycleRules: Receipts are stored per reviewer and commitment. Identical commitment bytes under another reviewer are a separate record.
ISSUE: nonzero commitment, zero replacement, never issued before by that reviewer. Creates Active with no links and issuedAt = updatedAt = block time.
REVOKE: zero replacement, target Active. Sets Revoked and updatedAt only.
SUPERSEDE: target Active; replacement nonzero, different and never issued by that reviewer. Old becomes Superseded with successor set; new becomes Active with predecessor set.
Revoked and Superseded are terminal. Nothing reactivates, overwrites or deletes an issued commitment; revoking a replacement does not restore its predecessor.
bytes32(0) is reserved for an absent link and an unused replacement field and is never issued.
Check order: action shape, zero reviewer, nonce, deadline, signature, then lifecycle. Any failure reverts everything, including the nonce.
A deadline limits when an action may execute. It does not expire an issued receipt.

nonces.model: One uint256 per reviewer, starting at zero, shared by ISSUE, REVOKE and SUPERSEDE. An action must carry exactly the current nonce and consumes exactly one.
nonces.cancellation: invalidateNonce(expectedNonce) advances only msg.sender's own nonce, requires an exact match and emits NonceInvalidated. A relayer cannot cancel for someone else.
nonces.exhaustion: At 2^256 - 1 both execute and invalidateNonce revert with NonceExhausted; the counter cannot wrap.
nonces.consequence: At most one outstanding signature per reviewer can ever execute; actions execute strictly in nonce order.

signatures.eoa: An address without code is checked with ECDSA recovery: 65-byte signatures only, low s, v of 27 or 28. ERC-2098 compact signatures are rejected.
signatures.contractAccount: An address with code is asked through an ERC-1271 STATICCALL. The reply must be at least 32 bytes and equal the magic value padded with zeros.
signatures.executor: Anyone may submit a signed action; msg.sender is never treated as the reviewer and there is no signature-free path.

decisions: Solidity 0.8.37: at the time of checking it was the only recent 0.8 release with no entry in the compiler's published known-bug list. EVM target osaka, because the Monad documentation states support for all opcodes and precompiles as of the Fusaka (Osaka) fork.
foundry.toml sets network = "monad" and Anvil runs with --network monad: the Monad documentation requires Foundry 1.8.0 or later with Monad execution enabled so local behaviour matches the chain.
Foundry is pinned by version, commit and per-platform archive SHA-256 in contracts/toolchain.json. Every invocation goes through contracts/scripts/foundry.ts, which refuses any other build.
Solidity libraries are installed by pnpm, not git submodules: OpenZeppelin from npm, forge-std from a git commit (the forge-std name on npm is an unrelated old package).
bytecode_hash is none so runtime code does not depend on local source paths. Runtime code still embeds chain- and address-specific immutables, so only the creation-code hash is predictable.
A fixed fuzz seed makes contract test runs reproducible.
The registry code lives at the @lexaegis/sdk/registry subpath so the root SDK entry stays free of viem.
Builders return the action with the chain and registry it was built for, and buildTypedData also takes the intended chain and registry and requires them to match.
JSON typed data includes the EIP712Domain type and uses decimal strings for chain ID, nonce and deadline; the action code is the number 0, 1 or 2.
Tests compute digests by hand, independently of hashAction, and read block time and chain ID through cheatcodes as Foundry's linter requires.
limitations: Local evidence only. The registry is not deployed anywhere; there is no address, and application configuration and readiness are unchanged.
Not audited. Negative controls were run by hand.
Foundry's Monad rules are an emulation, not the network.
An account with code is authorized only through ERC-1271. That includes an EOA carrying an EIP-7702 delegation: its plain ECDSA signature will not be accepted unless the delegate implements ERC-1271.
A contract account can make validation consume most of the gas an executor supplies. Only that executor is affected.
Because the nonce is sequential, two signed actions with the same nonce are alternatives: whichever executes first invalidates the other.
Monad block time is in whole seconds and several blocks share one timestamp, so issuedAt and updatedAt do not order events within a second.
The registry stores opaque commitments. It cannot show that an opening is truthful, complete or legally correct, or that a reviewer is a professional.
forge downloads solc 0.8.37 on first build. The toolchain installer supports Linux and macOS only.
laterDependencies: Chapter 5: preserve the encrypted opening and read it back before any receipt is published. A lost opening cannot be recovered from the chain.
Chapters 4 and 10: bind the explicit human approval to the PreparedReviewPackage and to the exact typed action shown to the reviewer. Signing consumes that snapshot; nothing rebuilds it.

Chapter 4: confirm how Mera accounts sign. If they are contract accounts or EIP-7702 delegated EOAs, the registry will call ERC-1271 isValidSignature with the plain EIP-712 digest; an account that wraps or re-hashes the digest needs matching support before it can authorize an action.

Chapters 4 and 6: read the current nonce and chain state immediately before signing. After a race or an InvalidNonce revert, re-read state and obtain a new signature; never blindly resubmit or auto-increment.

Chapter 6: deploy with contracts/script/DeployRegistry.s.sol, check the transaction input against creationCodeKeccak256, and write a deployed record that passes registryDeploymentSchema. Verify registry state at an identified block.
Chapters 6 and 11: a mined receipt means authorization was accepted when it executed. A later change to an ERC-1271 account's policy does not rewrite it and must not be read as invalidating it.
Chapter 7: Envio must reduce the four events without double counting (one SUPERSEDE is two logs, one new receipt) and reconcile indexed status with live registry reads; the live read wins.
Chapter 11: the verifier reports package integrity, receipt binding and lifecycle, and signer acceptance separately, and shows unknown for any failed read.

decisions: Mera has no abort signal, so Cancel discards the in-flight result by generation and never claims to have closed the browser prompt or removed a created passkey.
A dismissed prompt is reported as NOT_COMPLETED (dismissed, timed out or not allowed); only an AbortError cause or the application's own Cancel is CANCELLED.
Whether creation needed a fallback assertion is known only when the WebAuthn client is observable (tests); in the browser it is recorded as unknown, not as one prompt.
Backend session tokens are 256-bit random values stored as SHA-256 hashes; AUTH_SESSION_SECRET is unused.
Rate limiting is keyed by address, challenge and a global bucket in PostgreSQL; client IP is not used because forwarding headers are untrusted.
Feature flags and account configuration are passed from the server layout; the browser check builds into .next-check so it never replaces the normal build.
The Postgres launcher lives in root test-support so application tests do not import repository tooling.
Root engines.node is now >=24 because Mera requires it.
limitations: The derived key is a software key in page memory. Private fields, the CSP and buffer zeroing reduce exposure; they do not isolate it from a compromised same-origin script or dependency, and this is not a hardware-isolated wallet key.
Scope checks on signing are application code around an ordinary EOA key, not on-chain session-key restrictions.
Buffer zeroing is best effort; JavaScript and libraries may keep copies.
A passkey made for one rpId does not recover on another: localhost credentials are separate from any deployed domain, and a preview domain's credentials will not recover on the final domain.
No account rotation, administrator recovery or private-key export exists. Losing the passkey loses the account; a future evidence export does not restore a signing identity.
SIWE proves control of the address. It does not attest a biometric, a passkey provider or a professional identity.
Mera 0.2.0 is a preview dependency and has not been independently audited by this project.
One-prompt onboarding is not shown: the prompt count at create was not observed on the real device.
Synced cross-device recovery is not shown: no second device was available.

decisions: Embedded PostgreSQL plus VersityGW for tests, because Docker and MinIO were unavailable; production has no in-process fallback and missing configuration returns NOT_CONFIGURED.

Objects are immutable and written with If-None-Match: * (probed once per process). The catalog is a copy-on-write chain and the head moves only by compare-and-swap, so a lost acknowledgement is reconciled from the authoritative head instead of resent blindly.
A missing owned object is MISSING and a damaged one CORRUPT; an unreachable store is an outage and never 'not found'.

RecoverableCapture is unforgeable and non-serialisable, bound to account, vault and controller generation; it exists only after retrieval, authentication, decryption and Chapter 2 verification in the current unlock.
Imports are previewed first, re-encrypted under fresh IDs, salts and IVs for this vault, and never make the importer the reviewer.
Vault ID uniqueness is per-vault (composite primary key) so object IDs cannot be probed across accounts.
CLAUDE.md was cut to 426 words as the Chapter 5 prompt requires; the longer workflow detail is kept in the chapter prompts.
limitations: The service sees that an account has a vault, plus object counts, sizes and timing.
If all local state is lost, a replayed older snapshot cannot be detected; within a session or while an observed revision survives, regressions are reported.
A compromised same-origin script or dependency can reach unlocked data and the in-memory key.
Deleting a matter or context entry does not erase retained ciphertext, earlier exports or backups; there is no guaranteed erasure.
Recovery needs the original usable credential and rpId; a different passkey, a new passkey or another domain does not recover.
Quotas count unreferenced objects, so an interrupted save can consume space until cleanup tooling exists.
Hosting must allow 16 MiB request bodies on /api/vault/*/objects/* (Chapter 13).
Real-device and second-device recovery are unverified; no security audit is claimed.
Export/import on a real device not shown; readable-export disclosure preview not checked by the operator.

contracts.entryPoint: @lexaegis/agent/contracts (browser-safe); pure helpers in @lexaegis/agent/review; test fixtures in @lexaegis/agent/testing

schemas.request: lexaegis.assistant-request.v1 (clientRequestId, matterId, documentVersionId or null, snapshot digest and revision, vaultGeneration, intent or null, trigger, utterance, context, history, clientObserved, consent)
schemas.selectedContext: lexaegis.selected-context.v1 (sources as S1..Sn catalog entries holding the full SourceReferenceV1, confirmed facts, evidence selections, saved context, searchedScope with excerptsOnly)
schemas.consent: lexaegis.disclosure-consent.v1 (explicit_send, providerScope, matter, version, disclosureDigest over lexaegis.disclosure.v1)
schemas.toolResult: lexaegis.tool-result.v1 (handle T1..T8, tool version 1, outcome succeeded|failed|needs_narrowing, typed output per tool)
schemas.response: lexaegis.assistant-response.v1 (blocks explanation|quotation|calculation|finding|status referring to handles; fact proposals P1..P10; unresolved; questions; scope limitations; allowlisted next actions)
schemas.event: lexaegis.assistant-event.v1 (plan_updated, state_changed, tool_started, tool_result, response_delta, response_completed, output_reference, run_completed, run_cancelled, run_failed, run_interrupted; every event carries runId, matterId, documentVersionId, snapshotDigest, vaultGeneration, seq, timestamp)
schemas.runMetadata: lexaegis.agent-run-metadata.v1 (identifiers, state, outcome, deadlines, counters, usage provenance)

contracts.runStates: queued, running, stopping, completed, awaiting_input, cancelled, failed, interrupted; outcomes completed, needs_input, limited_scope, cancelled, failed, interrupted
contracts.limits: request 128 KiB, utterance 4 KiB, context 32 KiB, history 6 messages and 8 KiB, catalog 64 entries, quote 4 KiB, 8 answer blocks, 10 fact proposals, 10 unresolved items, output 32 KiB, tool arguments 4 KiB, tool result 16 KiB; overflow returns a typed code (limitCodeOf)
contracts.routing: routeUtterance: slash commands, unambiguous phrases, /stop to cancellation, approval or signing wording declined without a model; LOCAL_INTENTS (status, check_payments, missing_evidence) are served by browser code with no disclosure when asked for directly
decisions: Responses cite sources and tool results by handle only. The browser resolves handles through its own catalog and the tool_result events, so document text and computed values are never retyped by the model or retransmitted in an answer.
The snapshot digest travels in a consented request and in events; the server holds it in memory for the run and never stores it or sends it to the provider.
ReviewAgent.start returns admission metadata plus the live event stream; a repeated request ID returns the existing metadata with no stream and runs nothing.

disclosure.factsByIntent: summarise and explain send no facts; check_payments sends payment facts and the passages they cite; missing_evidence, prepare_review and brief_matter send all confirmed facts and the evidence links; client-observed status only for status, prepare_review and unclassified free text
disclosure.localOnly: A directly requested status, payment check or evidence check builds no request (LOCAL_INTENT) and discloses nothing
disclosure.savedContext: Only confirmed, explicitly ticked note or outcome entries; fact and evidence entries (typed prefixes) are refused as free text

prompts.words: common policy 463; with the largest intent asset 570 (limit 1,200)
prompts.hashing: SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 asset bytes; SHA-256 of RFC 8785 canonical JSON for the output, intent-selection and tool schemas; digests live in the manifest and the generated module, never inside hashed content
prompts.toolsByIntent: summarise: read_sources; explain: read_sources, get_rules; check_payments: read_sources, get_rules, check_payments; missing_evidence: read_sources, get_rules, check_evidence; brief_matter: read_sources, check_payments, check_evidence, get_status; prepare_review: get_rules, check_payments, check_evidence, prepare_review; status: get_status
decisions: The model is shown source handles and minimal metadata; excerpt text is read through read_sources, so every document read is a native tool call over the consented catalog.
Model output is a flat closed schema (provider keyword subset); handles are plain strings there and are resolved or rejected by code.
The server routes the utterance again and treats a claimed intent that contradicts it as unsupported.

provider.request: POST <base>/chat/completions with stream false, temperature 0, max_completion_tokens, enable_thinking false and enable_search false at the top level, parallel_tool_calls false whenever tools are offered, redirect error, no implicit retry, AbortSignal with a per-attempt timeout, response read capped at 128 KiB before parsing
provider.endpoints: https://<workspace>.<region>.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 for ap-southeast-1, us-east-1, cn-beijing, cn-hongkong, eu-central-1, ap-northeast-1, plus the three legacy dashscope hosts; anything else is CONFIG_INVALID
provider.outputMode: QWEN_OUTPUT_MODE json_schema (default, strict) or json_object (only when explicitly configured; the schema and the word JSON go in the prompt); never switched at run time
provider.failures: authentication, capability, rate_limit, timeout, transport, malformed_output, refusal, aborted; a length finish reason is reported as such and treated as a failure by the runtime
provider.capability: lexaegis.assistant-capability.v1: native tool call, structured output in the configured mode, usage reported, cancellation; verified needs the first, second and fourth; keyed by a SHA-256 fingerprint of provider, host, path, model and output mode
provider.testMode: LEXAEGIS_TEST_MODE=scripted-assistant with ASSISTANT_TEST_PROVIDER_URL on http://127.0.0.1:<port>/compatible-mode/v1; refused when QWEN_API_KEY is set; reported everywhere as provider scripted-test, region test-loopback
provider.newEnvironment: QWEN_OUTPUT_MODE, ASSISTANT_RUN_SECONDS, ASSISTANT_MAX_PROVIDER_ATTEMPTS, ASSISTANT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS, ASSISTANT_DAILY_RUNS_PER_ACCOUNT, ASSISTANT_DAILY_RUNS_GLOBAL, ASSISTANT_ACTIVE_RUNS_GLOBAL (all optional; ceilings can only be lowered)

tools.where: Tools run on the server over the consented SelectedContextV1 and the repository rule pack. The server has no vault and no full extraction, so read_sources returns catalog excerpts only and nothing can read further.
tools.adapters: read_sources: consented catalog; get_rules: toolGetRules with the pack's real review state (demo_draft); check_payments: toolReconcilePayments over confirmed facts in review mode; check_evidence: buildChecklist over the reviewer's links, scope stated; get_status: server readings plus client_observed readings, chain through a StatusPort, indexer not_connected, receipt not_selected; prepare_review: requirementsPreview, saved false and frozen false
tools.limits: arguments 4 KiB, result 16 KiB (needs_narrowing when larger, nothing partial), handles T1..T8, identical calls reuse the result within the run only
tools.notChanged: runChecks is not called by a tool because it needs the full verified extraction; the browser keeps running it locally

outputValidation.rejects: unknown or cross-run source and tool handles, unknown rules, failed tool results, a calculation without a check_payments result, a status without a get_status result, a quotation without exactly one source, a supported statement with no reference, an amount in pounds that no code result, confirmed fact or cited quote contains, invalid money or dates in a proposal (never coerced), extra fields, unknown actions, output over 32 KiB
outputValidation.demotes: a proposal with no source becomes an unresolved REVIEWER_STATEMENT_REQUIRED item
outputValidation.addsByCode: the excerpt-scope limitation on every answer built from excerpts; confirm_fact only when a proposal exists
outputValidation.repairCodes: compact machine codes only (for example UNKNOWN_SOURCE_HANDLE, OUTPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID:blocks.0.kind); they never contain case text
outputValidation.notAGuarantee: Validation shows reference integrity and schema conformance. It does not show that a statement follows from its citation, that a PDF was transcribed correctly or that anything is legally correct.

budget.ceilings: 6 provider attempts per run (routing, repair and retry included), 8 tool executions, 120 s per run, 25 s per attempt, 2,048 completion tokens per attempt, 8,192 per run, 65,536 reserved input tokens per attempt, 196,608 per run
budget.lowering: ASSISTANT_RUN_SECONDS, ASSISTANT_MAX_PROVIDER_ATTEMPTS and ASSISTANT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS can lower a ceiling; a higher or malformed value leaves the default; no request field can change one
budget.estimation: No verified matching tokenizer is installed, so input is reserved as UTF-8 bytes of the serialized messages, tools and response format plus a 4,096-token framing reserve, labelled conservative_utf8_bytes. max_completion_tokens is sent 10 tokens below the reservation for the documented tolerance.
budget.accounting: Reported usage replaces the reservation. Missing or aborted usage stays unknown and the reservation stays charged. One transient retry and one repair per run; a tool round starts only while an attempt and 2,048 output tokens remain for the final answer. No exact invoice cap is promised.

operationalStorage.tables: assistant_runs (id, owner, client_request_id, state, outcome, cancel_requested, lease_token, lease_expires_at, deadline_at, counters, usage_provenance, timestamps), assistant_quota (scope, utc_day, admitted), assistant_capability_checks (fingerprint, record, verified, checked_at)
operationalStorage.notStored: matter IDs, titles, document references, source hashes, snapshot digests, prompts, answers, tool payloads
operationalStorage.admission: one active run per account, three globally, 20 admitted per account per UTC day, 100 globally, decided in one transaction under an advisory lock; (owner, client_request_id) is unique and a repeat returns the existing run without running again
operationalStorage.leases: 15-second lease renewed by a 1-second heartbeat that also reads the durable cancellation flag; an expired lease becomes interrupted, never completed; terminal rows are removed after 24 hours and quota buckets after two UTC days
operationalStorage.terminal: finish is the single terminal transition, taken under a row lock by the lease holder; if cancellation was requested the run ends cancelled whatever the worker asked for

runtime.flow: consent digest and provider scope checked, then atomic admission, then routing (code first; one utterance-only completion only for unclassified free text), then either a direct code handler or tool rounds followed by one final round without tools and with the response format, then output validation and one terminal event
runtime.directHandlers: status always; check_payments and missing_evidence when sent as a command. They record modelExecution none and no provider section.
runtime.beforeEveryDispatch: stop observed, session still valid, lease renewed and durable cancel flag read, provider scope still equal to the consented one, budget reserved; the stop check and the dispatch are in the same tick, so nothing is sent after a stop is observed
runtime.toolRounds: at most one native call per completion; several calls in one completion are never executed (one repair, then PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS); an unknown or unauthorised tool or invalid arguments use the same single repair
runtime.cancellation: Stop sets the durable flag and aborts the in-process controller; the run enters stopping at once and ends cancelled only when the worker has acknowledged; if the answer was validated at the same moment it is discarded; a lost lease or unreachable store ends as interrupted with the provider outcome unknown
runtime.notDone: No automatic resume, replay or takeover after a restart; no persisted transcript; plaintext and the AbortController live in process memory only
runtime.completion: run_completed carries the AgentConfigV1 written from the execution: provider, requested and returned model, snapshot known or unknown, output mode, capability state, prompt and schema digests, parameters, budget and usage provenance

routes.GET /api/assistant: signed-in only; availability (not_configured, configured_unverified, verified, test_provider), provider scope (provider, model, endpoint region) and notices; no URL, workspace ID or credential
routes.POST /api/assistant/runs: session, exact configured Origin, application/json, X-LexAegis-Request: 1, 128 KiB body counted while read; body is the consented AssistantRequestV1 only; responds with text/event-stream (no-store, no-transform, X-Accel-Buffering: no), or JSON metadata for a repeated request ID
routes.GET /api/assistant/runs/[runId]: owner-bound operational metadata only; another account's run and a missing run are the same NOT_FOUND; no event replay
routes.POST /api/assistant/runs/[runId]/cancel: empty JSON object, 16 KiB limit; 202 while stopping, 200 with the terminal state once acknowledged; idempotent
routes.stream: frames are written only when the client reads (backpressure), 40 KiB frame bound, 15-second heartbeat comments that are not progress, contiguous seq as the SSE id, exactly one terminal event; client disconnect cancels the run
routes.logging: event name, request ID and a code only (assistant.run.started, .rejected, .repeated, .cancel); the logger has no parameter for bodies, headers or prompts; no tracing or error reporter is configured
routes.hosting: The request stays open for the run (at most 120 s; maxDuration 150). Verified locally on the Node server only. A host that cannot hold a streaming response that long is an integration blocker for Chapter 13; nothing falls back to background work.

browser.routing: The dock, slash commands, Explain selection and result actions go through one controller. /stop and Stop are handled by code. /status, /check-payments and /missing-evidence (typed or as an equivalent phrase) run on the device with no request. Everything else builds a disclosure preview; only its own Send creates consent and starts a run.
browser.states: The orb and the run cards show queued, working, stopping, finished, needs your input, failed, cancelled and interrupted from real events, each with text and an icon; the orb animates only while running or stopping and never under reduced motion (existing CSS).
browser.streamRules: Events are schema-validated; duplicates and events for another run, matter, version, snapshot or vault generation are dropped; a sequence gap, a malformed event, a block count mismatch or a stream that ends without a terminal event marks the result incomplete, cancels the run, reads operational status only and asks for a new request.
browser.clearing: Lock, account change or matter change clears the conversation, the pending disclosure and the excerpt catalog and abandons the run. A source, fact, evidence or selection revision stops the run, drops a pending disclosure and marks earlier results out of date.
browser.rendering: Model text is rendered as plain text by React (no HTML, Markdown or links). Quotations show the stored quote from the browser's own catalog; payment figures and status readings come from the tool result event. Citation buttons reopen the exact passage only if it still resolves against the current verified artifacts.
browser.notWired: Voice stays unavailable (Chapter 10). No approval control is enabled by a run.

proposalsAndSaving.confirmation: Only the Confirm control on a proposal card calls ReviewController.confirmFact, after the cited sources resolve again against the verified artifacts. It records the reviewer's account and time. A typed yes or approve, model output and imported JSON reach no confirmation path. A value for an already confirmed field is a correction (new revision); dependent results become out of date.
proposalsAndSaving.followUps: A follow-up uses the current matter, version and selection and a newly built disclosure. Free text that code cannot classify and that has no current selection is asked back once; an earlier passage, version or matter is never assumed.
proposalsAndSaving.saveOutcome: Explicit action only. The analysis artifact (lexaegis.assistant-analysis.v1) and the agent configuration are stored as immutable encrypted artifacts under version IDs fixed per result, read back through the vault and hash-checked, then an outcome entry (origin model_proposed, unconfirmed, typed prefix lexaegis.assistant-outcome.v1:) is committed with saveMatter. Saved is shown only after the entry is present in the committed record. A failed write leaves the result on screen as unsaved; a retry completes the vault's pending commit instead of storing twice.
proposalsAndSaving.kept: Raw chat is never stored. Unconfirmed proposals are not written into the analysis artifact. A saved outcome can become request context only after the reviewer confirms the entry with the existing vault controls.
proposalsAndSaving.observedVaultBehaviour: A failed addSourceFile leaves the source in the working draft with its sealed object held in the vault's pending commit; reconcile completes it. Calling saveMatter instead would start a new commit without that object, so the assistant never does that for an unfinished artifact.

provenance.agentConfig: lexaegis.agent-config.v1: profile, runtime version, modelExecution (qwen, scripted-test or none), provider region, requested and returned model, model snapshot known or explicitly unknown, output mode, capability state and check time, provider request IDs, prompt manifest version with common-policy, intent-asset, output-schema and tool-schema SHA-256 digests, fixed generation parameters, the run budget, usage with provenance, run ID, intent, start and finish time, outcome. A code-only or device-local run records modelExecution none with no provider, prompts or parameters and usage none.
provenance.analysis: lexaegis.assistant-analysis.v1: validated blocks, unresolved items, questions, scope limitations, only the sources, rules and tool results the answer cites, the input snapshot digest, the run facts and three fixed limitations. No hidden reasoning, credential, endpoint, transcript or provider request or response; unconfirmed proposals are counted, not stored.
provenance.bytes: RFC 8785 canonical JSON hashed with SHA-256 through Chapter 2's functions. The same run gives the same bytes; recorded timestamps and IDs are never regenerated. Model output is not deterministic even with fixed parameters; only hashing, validation and code calculations are.
provenance.draft: ReviewController.draftArtifacts({ analysisVersionId, agentConfigVersionId }) reads both back through the vault and passes the exact bytes to assembleDraft, which requires canonical bytes of the expected schemas, the same run and matter, the current snapshot digest, every cited source and rule in the draft, and cited payment results equal to the draft's own. Failures: AGENT_ARTIFACT_INVALID, AGENT_ARTIFACT_STALE, AGENT_ARTIFACT_MISMATCH, MISSING_DEPENDENCY. Roles used: agent-config and analysis (existing v1 roles). AGENT_CONFIG_MISSING is cleared only then; DECISION_LOG_MISSING and HUMAN_REVIEW_GATE_PENDING always remain.
provenance.notDone: No freeze, opening nonce, decision log, approval instruction or transaction. prepare_review returns requirements only.

decisions: The Chapter 8 comparison test in pipeline.test.ts (an edit-distance abort that takes about a second of CPU against a two-second wall-clock limit) reported timeout instead of edit distance in most fully parallel runs once this chapter's integration tests were added, and in the readiness gate. Its edit-distance step now runs with the Date clock frozen, so it tests that limit and not machine load; the assertion is unchanged. With that the suite passed three times under the gate's parallel load at the default worker count. An interim cap on test workers was removed again.
